title: AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning
subtopics: AI systems that do not learn from data
Machine learning as a subset of AI
Deep learning as a subset of machine learning
learning_outcomes: Explain aI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning and connect at least two of its listed subtopics.
Apply the central idea in aI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning to a small example or select a suitable approach for a stated scenario.
Identify an important assumption, failure mode, risk, or limitation and describe how it should be checked.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study aI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning within History, Categories, and Approaches to AI. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: AI contains multiple traditions and capability labels. Compare systems by what they do, how they work, and the evidence available—not by hype.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: AI is the broad field; machine learning is an approach within AI in which parameters are fit from data; deep learning is a machine-learning family based on multilayer neural networks. Some AI systems use no learned model at all.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Identify what ai, machine learning, and deep learning takes as input and what result or decision it is intended to support. 2. Read the example before running it and predict the output. 3. Run the small example, compare actual and expected output, then change one input or assumption and repeat. 4. Record what the example demonstrates and what it does not demonstrate about a real system.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. AI contains multiple traditions and capability labels. Compare systems by what they do, how they work, and the evidence available—not by hype.

content_blocks.code:
inputs = [0.5, 1.0]
weights = [2.0, -1.0]
bias = 0.25
score = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(inputs, weights)) + bias
relu = max(0.0, score)
print("score:", round(score, 2))
print("relu:", round(relu, 2))
content_blocks.run_instructions: Copy the code into a local file named main.py and run `python main.py` with Python 3. Compare the printed output with the expected result documented here. This CodeLeaf content block is static; it does not execute the snippet in the browser and needs no external API key.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet or return to the small synthetic input, rerun it, and change one value at a time. Do not add real credentials, private user data, or untrusted code to the example.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. If the example runs as expected, do not infer that it proves a trained model works; this snippet is a deterministic teaching aid. Keep sensitive data out of tests.

content_blocks.title: Check before you trust a result
content_blocks.text: This is a small, deterministic teaching example—not a trained AI model or evidence of production performance. Run it with a local Python 3 interpreter; do not paste secrets or private data into experiments.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: AI is the broad field; machine learning is an approach within AI in which parameters are fit from data; deep learning is a machine-learning family based on multilayer neural networks. Some AI systems use no learned model at all. Next, connect this lesson to its prerequisite or next lesson and carry the same habit forward: define success, test a representative case, inspect failures, and document limitations.

content.task: Try it yourself: take five example systems related to ai, machine learning, and deep learning. Classify each by its task, input, output, and AI approach; justify one ambiguous case and state evidence that would change your classification.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core concept and accurately refer to the source syllabus topics.
Record a prediction and compare it with a reproducible result or a clearly stated manual trace.
Document at least one limitation, safety consideration, or evaluation requirement.
hints: Write down the inputs, expected output, and assumptions before changing the example.
Change only one input or condition and compare the results with your original prediction.
Ask whether the example covers realistic cases, important subgroups, and failure conditions; a toy example does not establish production reliability.
troubleshooting: Use Python 3 and run the file from the folder where it was saved.
If output differs, restore the original input and compare one changed value at a time.
If Python reports a syntax error, check copied quotation marks, indentation, and whether the full code block was copied.
These examples require no external packages, network access, model credentials, or personal data.
